accountingIdentity.function: annihilateFrom(address stable, address from, address recipient, uint256 amount)
derivation: 1. stableAmount = toStableAmount(stable, amount) = amount / 10**(18-decimals), and the call REVERTS unless stableAmount * 10**(18-decimals) == amount exactly (src/Antimatter.sol:254-256). So stableAmount is an EXACT rescale of `amount`; exchangeRate plays NO part in how much stablecoin is pulled.
3. stableAmount of `stable` is pulled from `from` (src/Antimatter.sol:222) and pushed into PhusdStableMinter.mint (src/Antimatter.sol:227).

4. PhusdStableMinter.calculateMintAmount (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:254-255) returns (stableAmount * exchangeRate * 10**(18-decimals)) / 1e18. Substituting stableAmount * 10**(18-decimals) == amount from step 1, this equals (amount * exchangeRate) / 1e18, truncated down.
5. The minter mints that phUSD to msg.sender, i.e. to Antimatter itself (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:232 `IMintableToken(phUSD).mint(msg.sender, phUSDAmount)`).
6. mintedForStable is MEASURED as a balance delta, not assumed (src/Antimatter.sol:232), and must be non-zero (:233).
7. Antimatter then mints `amount` phUSD directly to recipient (src/Antimatter.sol:236) and forwards mintedForStable (:237).
accountingIdentity.identity: phUSD_out(recipient) = amount + floor(amount * exchangeRate / 1e18);  stable_in = amount / 10**(18-decimals);  antimatter_burned = amount

mintedForStableEqualsAmount.answer: NO — only when exchangeRate == 1e18. It diverges whenever the stable minter's owner sets a non-unit rate.
mintedForStableEqualsAmount.evidence: PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner and unbounded (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:138-143). The antimatter project ITSELF asserts the divergence is intended: test/Annihilation.t.sol:107-116 sets rate 0.95e18 and asserts recipient gets 195e18, not 200e18 ('A non-1:1 exchange rate is the stable minter's business').

accountingIdentity.asymmetry: The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (pure decimal rescale, src/Antimatter.sol:254-255) while the phUSD MINTED for that leg is rate-scaled. The antimatter leg is ALWAYS exactly `amount` phUSD regardless of rate (src/Antimatter.sol:236). Therefore at exchangeRate > 1e18 the pair emits more than 2x phUSD per unit of stablecoin taken in, and at rate < 1e18 less. Rate is a single owner-settable knob with no bounds check anywhere on either side.
accountingIdentity.rounding: Single truncation, inside calculateMintAmount (integer division by 1e18). Rounds DOWN, i.e. in the protocol's favour on the stable leg. toStableAmount refuses to round at all — it reverts on a non-representable amount (src/Antimatter.sol:256) rather than burning antimatter the stablecoin half cannot match.

stableLeg.backedBy: The stablecoin actually deposited: stableAmount is transferred to PhusdStableMinter and then into IYieldStrategy.deposit(stable, stableAmount, address(minter)) (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:229). Principal is credited to the MINTER, not to the annihilator or to Antimatter.
stableLeg.caveat: The deposited stable is booked as strategy principal for the minter; it is not redeemable by the phUSD holder from Antimatter. Antimatter has no withdraw path at all.

antimatterLeg.backedBy: NOTHING is transferred in for this leg. Antimatter mints it out of thin air at src/Antimatter.sol:236. Its only 'backing' is the destruction of `amount` antimatter at src/Antimatter.sol:215.
antimatterLeg.consequence: phUSD collateralisation is therefore a direct function of antimatter emission discipline. Every antimatter token in existence is a standing claim on 1e18 of uncollateralised phUSD, redeemable by anyone holding it plus a matching stablecoin. Antimatter supply is unbounded: mint() (src/Antimatter.sol:179) has no cap, no schedule, and no total-supply ceiling, and is callable by the owner OR any address in _approvedMinters.

externalCallOrdering.note: Reads yieldStrategy/decimals from the minter. Trusted-config read; a hostile minter could lie about decimals, but the minter is owner-set.
Pre-image for the mintedForStable delta. Correctly EXCLUDES any phUSD donated to Antimatter beforehand — a donation is not swept to the first annihilator, it stays stuck and is rescueERC20-able.

externalCallOrdering.reentrancySurface: YES — arbitrary token code runs here. `stable` is constrained only by being registered with the minter, so it is owner-vetted, not arbitrary user input. Guarded by nonReentrant; the project proves this with a hostile _update-hook token at test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol:25-31 + test/Annihilation.t.sol:276.

Nested: minter pulls the stable (PhusdStableMinter.sol:226) then calls IYieldStrategy.deposit (:229) then IMintableToken(phUSD).mint (:232). Minter is itself nonReentrant (:203); the strategy is nonReentrant on both pinned and master vault trees.

externalCallOrdering.note: Approval is always zeroed on the success path — no standing allowance is left to the minter.
Strict equality against stableBefore. Reverts StableNotDeposited on ANY residue — this is what makes fee-on-transfer / rebasing stables fail closed rather than strand dust.
mintedForStable = delta; must be > 0 (:233). Note this measures ANY phUSD that arrived during steps 4-7, not strictly what the minter minted.

externalCallOrdering.reentrancySurface: FlaxToken._mint is plain OZ ERC20 with no hooks (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58-69) — no callback to recipient.
None — plain OZ ERC20 transfer, no hooks.

reentrancySurfaceSummary.guard: OZ ReentrancyGuard, non-transient (OZ 5.6.1 ReentrancyGuard, not ReentrancyGuardTransient) — confirmed by import at src/Antimatter.sol:8.
reentrancySurfaceSummary.crossFunctionReentrancy: mint() (:179) is NOT nonReentrant, but has no external call and cannot be reached by an unauthorised reenterer; rescueERC20 (:263) IS nonReentrant. There is no read-only view whose value another contract could act on mid-annihilation — Antimatter holds no user accounting beyond ERC20 balances, which are already fully settled (burn at :215) before any external call.
reentrancySurfaceSummary.residualSurface: A hostile `stable` re-entering PhusdStableMinter.mint DIRECTLY (bypassing Antimatter's guard) during step 4 is not blocked by Antimatter's guard, but at that instant the minter's own nonReentrant is not yet engaged either, so it is indistinguishable from an ordinary third-party mint. It cannot touch Antimatter's in-flight state because that state (the burn) is already final.

whoCanMintAntimatter.answer: Antimatter.owner() (constructor-set, transferable via OZ Ownable) OR any address in _approvedMinters.
whoCanMintAntimatter.evidence: src/Antimatter.sol:112 modifier onlyApprovedMinters; src/Antimatter.sol:179 mint(). Set membership is owner-controlled via setApprovedMinter (:151). Note the owner mints WITHOUT appearing in approvedMinters() — the enumerable set is not a complete authority list (documented at :158).
whoCanMintAntimatter.bounds: None. No supply cap, no per-period cap, no schedule.

whoCanMintPhUSD.answer: Any address with FlaxToken._authorizedMinters[a].canMint == true AND matching mintVersion.
whoCanMintPhUSD.evidence: lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58-69 (`require(minterInfo.canMint)` + `require(minterInfo.mintVersion == mintVersion)`); set by FlaxToken.setMinter, onlyOwner (:44-51).
whoCanMintPhUSD.requiredForAnnihilation: YES — Antimatter itself MUST be an authorised phUSD minter, otherwise src/Antimatter.sol:236 reverts and the whole annihilation rolls back. PhusdStableMinter must ALSO be one, for src/Antimatter.sol:227 to succeed. Both authorisations are required, and both are held by FlaxToken's owner, not by Antimatter's owner. Test setup makes this explicit: test/Annihilation.t.sol:40-41 authorises both; test/Annihilation.t.sol:248 revokes Antimatter's and asserts full rollback.
whoCanMintPhUSD.globalKillSwitch: FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges() (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:88-91) increments mintVersion, silently invalidating BOTH Antimatter and PhusdStableMinter in one owner call. It emits no per-minter event; the two contracts have no view that reflects their own de-authorisation.

whoOwnsTheStableMinter.answer: PhusdStableMinter.owner(), set to msg.sender at deploy (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:66) — an INDEPENDENT owner from Antimatter.owner() and from FlaxToken.owner(). Nothing in any of the three contracts requires them to be the same principal.
powersThatReachIntoAnnihilation: registerStablecoin (:111) — decides what may be annihilated at all; Antimatter deliberately keeps no list (src/Antimatter.sol:250 reads the minter's).
updateExchangeRate (:138) — unilaterally re-prices the stable leg of every future annihilation, unbounded, no timelock, no event-driven grace period.
setMaxMintPerDay (:190) — throttles annihilation volume for a given stable.
setPauser (:76) / pauser.pause (:86) — global annihilation kill switch. Test asserts full rollback at test/Annihilation.t.sol:262.

approveYS (:180) — a stablecoin that has NOT been approveYS'd will make PhusdStableMinter.mint revert at :229, bricking annihilation for that stable even though it is 'registered' as far as Antimatter's toStableAmount check (src/Antimatter.sol:251) is concerned.

antimatterOwnerPowers: setPhUSD (:124) — cannot drift from the minter: refuses any phUSD the already-set minter does not mint (:127-129).

setPhUSDMinter (:136) — requires phUSD set first and requires newMinter.phUSD() == phUSD (:139-141). It does NOT constrain the new minter's stablecoin set, exchange rates or caps, so repointing swaps the whole pricing regime in one call.
authorizationGraph.graphSummary: Three mutually independent owners. Antimatter.owner controls antimatter supply and which minter is used; PhusdStableMinter.owner controls the exchange rate, the supported-stable list and the daily cap; FlaxToken.owner controls whether either contract may mint phUSD at all. An annihilation succeeds only if all three are simultaneously cooperative, plus the yield strategy (which must have PhusdStableMinter as an authorised client and must not be paused).

localFindings.description: An ERC20 allowance over ANTIMATTER is silently also an authority to spend the grantor's STABLECOIN and to redirect all resulting value. If Alice approves Antimatter for her USDC (which she must, to annihilate at all: `The stablecoin is always pulled from `from``, :195-196) and separately grants Bob an antimatter allowance of N, Bob may call annihilateFrom(usdc, alice, bob, N): :214 spends only the antimatter allowance, :222 pulls N-worth of Alice's USDC on Antimatter's own standing approval, and :236-237 send the entire ~2N phUSD to `recipient`, which is caller-chosen and unrelated to `from`. Bob converts Alice's stablecoin at her expense and keeps the proceeds. No stablecoin allowance to Bob is ever required and no second signature from Alice is involved.
localFindings.why_local: Fully determined inside Antimatter.sol: the allowance check at :214 covers one asset, the debit at :222 covers a second, and the credit at :236-237 goes to a third-party-chosen address. No cross-contract behaviour is needed to see it.
localFindings.recommendation: Either force recipient == from when msg.sender != from, or require the caller to hold a matching stablecoin allowance from `from`, or document the antimatter allowance explicitly as a dual-asset authority.

localFindings.description: PhusdStableMinter's rolling 24h issuance cap (maxMintPerDay, lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:215-223) is charged ONLY for the stable leg — it counts phUSDAmount, the amount the minter itself mints. The antimatter leg at src/Antimatter.sol:236 is minted by Antimatter directly against its own FlaxToken authorisation and is invisible to that accounting. An annihilation therefore issues `amount + amount*rate/1e18` phUSD while consuming only `amount*rate/1e18` of the cap. At the intended 1:1 rate the cap governs exactly half the phUSD it was configured to govern; an operator who sets maxMintPerDay = X to bound daily phUSD issuance actually permits 2X.
localFindings.why_local: The bypass is created by Antimatter's own decision to mint the second leg itself rather than route both through the capped path; the evidence is one line in this contract plus the cap's own definition.
localFindings.footgunTest: A competent, non-malicious operator setting a daily issuance cap WOULD be surprised that the effective cap is double the number they entered. Law-3 footgun, in scope.
localFindings.recommendation: Either charge the antimatter leg against the minter's cap, or add an equivalent cap on Antimatter's own leg, or rename/document the minter cap as a per-stable deposit cap rather than a phUSD-issuance cap.

localFindings.description: EnumerableSet.values() copies the whole set to memory with no bound. External view only, so no on-chain caller is forced through it, but it will gas-out for an off-chain reader once the set grows large, and any future on-chain consumer inherits an unbounded loop.
localFindings.recommendation: Paginate, or keep approvedMinterAt/approvedMinterCount (:169, :164) as the supported iteration path and document values() as off-chain-only.

localFindings.description: mintedForStable is a balance DELTA over the window :220-:232, not an attribution of what PhusdStableMinter minted for this call. Any phUSD that reaches Antimatter during steps 4-7 — e.g. a yield strategy or a hostile registered `stable` that pushes phUSD to Antimatter from its transfer hook — is counted as part of the stable leg and forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient at :237. The measured-balance pattern is the right instinct (it is what makes :230 fail closed), but on the phUSD side it converts any concurrent inbound phUSD into free value for whoever is annihilating. `stable` is owner-registered rather than arbitrary, which is what holds this to Low.
localFindings.recommendation: Attribute the stable leg from minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) and use the balance delta only as an equality assertion, so an unexpected inbound is a revert rather than a windfall.

localFindings.description: The stable leg's size is a linear function of an unbounded, un-timelocked, single-call owner parameter, while the stablecoin actually taken in is rate-INDEPENDENT (src/Antimatter.sol:254-255 uses decimals only). At exchangeRate > 1e18 the pair emits more than 2x phUSD per unit of stablecoin taken in, further diluting the already-unbacked antimatter leg. Antimatter applies no sanity bound of its own even though it reads the config struct at :250 and could. Recorded here as the local half of what is fundamentally an interaction/econ concern.
localFindings.recommendation: Bound the rate in toStableAmount (or assert mintedForStable is within a tolerance of `amount`) so a fat-fingered rate cannot silently double phUSD issuance.

nonFindings: Fee-on-transfer / rebasing stables: fail CLOSED, not silently. :222 pulls less than stableAmount, :227 then reverts inside the minter's own safeTransferFrom, and even if it did not, :230's strict equality catches any residue. Also a C4 known-invalid class.
Stablecoins with >18 decimals: rejected explicitly at src/Antimatter.sol:252 (UnsupportedDecimals) before the minter's own 10**(18-decimals) would underflow-revert. Consistent, fails closed.
exchangeRate == 0: mintedForStable == 0 -> PhUSDNotReceived revert at :233. Liveness only, no value loss.
phUSD donated to Antimatter before an annihilation: excluded by the phUSDBefore snapshot at :220, so it is not swept to the annihilator. Recoverable via rescueERC20 (:263).
rescueERC20 owner sweep: obvious owner power, Law-3 suppressed.

rescueERC20(IERC20 token, address to, uint256 amount)

externalCalls.notes: Owner-set and cross-checked against the minter's phUSD() at :127-129 and :139-141, so it cannot drift. Plain OZ ERC20 with no transfer hooks (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol) — no inbound-callback surface. Antimatter must be an authorised minter on it or annihilation reverts at :236.

Sole source of truth for supported stables, decimals, exchange rate, daily cap and pause. Its owner is a DIFFERENT principal from Antimatter's owner and can re-price or halt annihilation unilaterally.

Not arbitrary user input — must be registered with the minter (:251), i.e. owner-vetted. Executes arbitrary code inside :222, which is the primary reentrancy surface; guarded and regression-tested (test/Annihilation.t.sol:276).

Caller-chosen and unconstrained apart from != 0 (:207). Receives value via phUSD mint/transfer, which run no callback, so it is a value-redirection surface (see AM-LOCAL-001) rather than a reentrancy one.

externalCalls.target: IYieldStrategy (reached transitively, never called by Antimatter)
externalCalls.notes: See IYieldStrategy.json. Antimatter never holds its address and never calls it; it is reached only inside PhusdStableMinter.mint.

trustAssumptions: Antimatter AND PhusdStableMinter are both currently-versioned authorised minters on FlaxToken. FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges (lib/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:88-91) de-authorises both in one call with no per-minter event; annihilation then reverts wholesale (test/Annihilation.t.sol:248).

PhusdStableMinter is an authorised CLIENT on the yield strategy (AYieldStrategy.deposit is onlyAuthorizedClient) and the strategy is not paused — otherwise every annihilation of that stable reverts at PhusdStableMinter.sol:229.

The stable has been approveYS'd (PhusdStableMinter.sol:180). Antimatter's own registration check (:251) tests only yieldStrategy != 0 and will happily pass a registered-but-unapproved stable straight into a revert.
exchangeRate is intended to be ~1e18. Nothing enforces it on either side; Antimatter explicitly forwards whatever the minter produced (test/Annihilation.t.sol:105-116).

Antimatter has no pause of its own. Halting annihilation requires action by PhusdStableMinter's pauser, PhusdStableMinter's owner (setStablecoinEnabled), or FlaxToken's owner — none of which are Antimatter's owner.
The antimatter leg of phUSD is structurally uncollateralised; solvency of the phUSD system depends on antimatter emission being controlled off-contract, since mint() has no cap.

STALE-PIN CAVEAT: PhusdStableMinter discards IYieldStrategy.deposit's return value. On the vault tree the minter is pinned to (lib/.../vault @ 043ff2c) deposit returns nothing, so this is consistent. On vault master (0110ce4, story-049) deposit returns creditedPrincipal, which may be strictly LESS than `amount` (conservative convertToAssets crediting, stories 043/044/049). Solidity ignores surplus returndata, so there is no ABI brick — but the phUSD minted for the stable leg is computed from `amount`, never from creditedPrincipal, so on the deployed (master) vault the stable leg can be minted against principal that was never fully credited. Adjudicating that is interaction-level; recorded here as an assumption.

treeProvenance.note: There is NO top-level lib/phUSD-stable-minter or lib/flax-token-v2 sibling submodule in this audit repo (`ls lib/` at /home/justin/code/audits lists only antimatter, forge-std, openzeppelin-contracts, phlimbo-ea, phoenix-nft-staking, phoenix-phase-2-staging, reflax-yield-vault, stable-staker, stable-yield-accumulator, yield-claim-nft). Every claim about PhusdStableMinter, FlaxToken and IYieldStrategy in this profile was therefore read from antimatter's OWN nested pins, which are stale by construction. Where the staleness matters it is called out explicitly (see trustAssumptions STALE-PIN CAVEAT and IYieldStrategy.json).
